h1: The 6 Best Electric Kettles for Pour-Over Coffee, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Pour-Over Electric Kettles: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 gooseneck electric kettles for pour-over coffee, scored on spout control, temperature precision, capacity and build quality.
summary: The Fellow Stagg EKG Pro is the electric gooseneck to buy if pour-over is a daily ritual, with a 0.9L body shaped around a controlled stream. The INTASTING offers 1 degree temperature control for far less, and the Cosori Gooseneck is the dependable middle. The Fellow Corvo Studio is the glass showpiece, while the DmofwHi and Bodum are the budget ways to get a gooseneck.
intro: Pour-over coffee is decided in the first thirty seconds. You wet the grounds slowly, let them bloom, then pour in a thin, steady spiral, and a kettle that dumps water in a rush ruins that routine no matter how good your beans are. A gooseneck spout fixes the pour, but it fixes only half the problem, because water that is a few degrees too hot or too cool changes what you taste.

So the ranking weighs two things above all: how steadily each kettle pours and how precisely it can hold a temperature. Capacity and body material come next. Every pick here has a gooseneck spout, which is the entry requirement, and we left out standard-spout kettles because they cannot do the job. Where a listing gave no temperature detail, we marked it down.

products.name: Fellow Stagg EKG Pro Gooseneck Electric Kettle
products.verdict: The kettle made for pour-over, with a 0.9L body and a refined gooseneck.
products.description:
Fellow designed the Stagg EKG Pro around one job: pouring for coffee. The kettle holds 0.9L, has a gooseneck spout, and sits in the $100 to $200 tier, the second highest price in this ranking.

Its position is earned by design focus. Where the Cosori and the DmofwHi are kettles with a gooseneck added, the Stagg is a pour-over tool that happens to boil water, and the shape of the spout and handle reflect that. At 0.9L it holds enough for a large dripper with a spare cup. The INTASTING offers temperature precision for less, so the case for the Stagg rests on handling.

Buy it if you brew pour-over every morning and want it to feel good. The caveat is the price, which pays for ergonomics more than for a hotter or faster boil.
products.idealFor: Daily pour-over brewers who value feel and ritual.
products.skipIf: You want the most temperature precision for the money.

products.name: INTASTING Gooseneck Electric Kettle with 1℉ Temperature Control
products.verdict: A 0.9L stainless gooseneck that sets temperature in 1 degree steps.
products.description:
The INTASTING is a 0.9L stainless steel gooseneck kettle with temperature control in 1 degree Fahrenheit steps. It sits in the $50 to $100 tier.

Step size is the useful number. Many kettles offer presets for tea types, while 1 degree control lets you land at 200 degrees for a light roast or 195 for a dark one and repeat it every morning. That repeatability is what pour-over brewers chase, and it is why this kettle outranks the Cosori. It ranks below the Stagg because the listing details less about the pour and the handle, and the Stagg has the stronger coffee pedigree.

Buy it if you tune your water temperature by roast. The caveat is brand track record, which is shorter than Fellow's.
products.idealFor: Brewers who tune water temperature to the roast.
products.skipIf: You want a coffee-specialist brand and handling.

products.name: Cosori Gooseneck Electric Kettle with Temperature Control
products.verdict: A 0.8L stainless gooseneck with temperature control at a mid-range price.
products.description:
Cosori's gooseneck kettle holds 0.8L in a stainless steel body, with a narrow spout and temperature control. It sits in the $50 to $100 tier.

It earns third place on balance. The temperature control is there for brewing at the right heat, and the stainless interior avoids plastic taste, which matters for a drink as delicate as a light roast. At 0.8L it is the smallest of the temperature-controlled picks, so a larger dripper may need a refill. Against the INTASTING, it is similar in price but gives less step precision.

Buy it if you want a proven, simple pour-over kettle without paying the Fellow premium. The caveat is the capacity, which limits big batches.
products.idealFor: Home brewers who want temperature settings without a big spend.
products.skipIf: You brew large batches in one pour.

products.name: Fellow Corvo EKG Pro Studio Gooseneck Electric Kettle
products.verdict: A glass-bodied Fellow gooseneck that lets you watch the water.
products.description:
The Corvo EKG Pro Studio is a glass gooseneck electric kettle from Fellow, in the $200 to $500 tier, the most expensive pick here.

Glass is the difference. It lets you see the water and any mineral build-up, and it adds a visual feel that stainless cannot. It ranks fourth, below the three stainless models, because the price is the highest in the ranking and the listing states no capacity or temperature detail to justify it. Against the Stagg, the same brand's cheaper option, it asks you to pay more for the material.

Buy it if the kettle sits on display and you value design. The caveat is that glass can break, and you are paying a premium without clear performance gains.
products.idealFor: Design-minded brewers who want a kettle on show.

products.name: DmofwHi Gooseneck Electric Kettle
products.verdict: A 1L stainless gooseneck that costs under $50.
products.description:
The DmofwHi is a 1L stainless steel gooseneck kettle in the $25 to $50 tier, with the largest capacity of the gooseneck group.

Its 1L volume lets you brew a full 600ml pour-over with water to spare, and the stainless body is the right material. What it lacks, going by the listing, is any stated temperature control, so you rely on boiling and letting the water rest a short while before pouring. That is a workable habit but not as repeatable as the INTASTING's 1 degree steps.

Buy it if you want to try pour-over cheaply. The caveat is that the lack of temperature control and sparse detail make it a starter kettle.
products.idealFor: Beginners trying pour-over on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You want to repeat an exact brewing temperature.

products.name: Bodum 27oz Bistro Gooseneck Electric Water Kettle
products.verdict: A compact 27oz stainless gooseneck for a single cup at a time.
products.description:
The Bodum Bistro is a 27oz stainless steel gooseneck kettle in the $25 to $50 tier, close to 0.8L.

It is the smallest on the list, and for a single-cup dripper that's a fair fit. You fill, boil, pour, and the compact body takes little counter space. It ranks last because the listing states no temperature control, and a 27oz capacity leaves little room if you brew two cups. Compared with the DmofwHi, it carries less water at a similar price.

Buy it if you brew one cup at a time in a small kitchen. The caveat is that there is no margin for a second pour without a refill.
products.skipIf: You brew two cups or more.

methodology.description: Every pick has a gooseneck, and we ranked on how the listing describes the spout and handle for steady pouring.

methodology.description: Stainless steel and glass were compared on taste, durability and appearance.

methodology.description: We weighed price tier against what the kettle adds for coffee, not general boiling.

whatMatters.detail: A pour-over needs a thin, slow stream to wet grounds evenly, and a gooseneck spout delivers it. A wide spout floods the bed and causes uneven extraction. Look for gooseneck in the title, and check whether the handle balances the weight so your wrist stays steady during a three-minute pour.

Coffee extracts differently at different heat: light roasts like hotter water, dark roasts cooler. A kettle with fine steps, like the INTASTING's 1 degree, repeats a recipe exactly. Look for the step size in the listing and whether it holds temperature after reaching it.

A single-cup drip needs about 300ml of water, a large dripper 600ml or more. A kettle should hold enough for the bloom and the pour with some spare. Compare the liters on the listing to your dripper, and remember that kettles boil more efficiently when well filled.

Water touches the interior for minutes, so material affects taste. Stainless steel and glass do not carry flavor, while plastic can. Look for a stainless or glass interior in the description, and avoid kettles where the lid or spout is plastic and sits in contact with hot water.

A full kettle held out at arm's length tires the wrist, and a shaky wrist ruins a controlled pour. Handle shape, counterweight and base design matter more than they seem. Look for reviews and photos showing a grip you can hold with a thumb on top, and test the balance when it arrives.

faq.q: Do I need a gooseneck kettle for pour-over?
faq.a: For good results, yes. A gooseneck meters a thin stream so grounds wet evenly. Every pick here has one, from the budget DmofwHi to the Fellow Stagg EKG Pro, and a standard kettle will pour too fast.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with pour-over kettles?
faq.a: Brewing with boiling water for every roast. Too-hot water over-extracts dark roasts and tastes bitter. The INTASTING's 1 degree steps and the Cosori's temperature control let you drop to a better heat.

faq.q: Is the Fellow Stagg worth it over the Cosori?
faq.a: If pour-over is a daily ritual, yes. The Stagg EKG Pro is built for handling and costs more, while the Cosori Gooseneck gives temperature control and a 0.8L body for much less.

faq.q: How do I set up the brew?
faq.a: Set the kettle to your temperature, rinse the filter, add grounds, then pour a small bloom and wait thirty seconds. Finish in slow circles. The Stagg and INTASTING hold 0.9L, enough for a large dripper.

Monthly in hard water areas, less in soft. Boil a vinegar and water mix, rest, rinse. The Corvo's glass body shows scale clearly, while stainless models such as the DmofwHi hide it, so check by sight.

faq.q: Can I use these kettles for tea?
faq.a: Yes. The Cosori and INTASTING temperature control suits green and oolong tea, which should not meet a full boil. The 1L DmofwHi works for black tea, but with no temperature setting.

finalTake: The Fellow Stagg EKG Pro is the best electric kettle for pour-over coffee, because its whole design serves the pour. The INTASTING is the smart alternative, with 1 degree steps for a lower price, and the Cosori Gooseneck is the dependable middle. The Corvo is a premium glass choice. If you're just starting, the DmofwHi gets you a gooseneck cheaply.
